title: Multi-omics characterization of different dietary fiber levels on microbiota and metabolism in Erhualian and large white pigs.
authors: Du Taoran; Zheng Chuanxia; Hao Yun; Niu Qing; Xu Liming et al.
abstract:
UNLABELLED: Erhualian pigs (EHL) exhibit tolerance to high-fiber diets, yet the underlying mechanisms involving gut microbiota and metabolism remain unclear. Here, we integrated colonic short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) profiling, 16S rRNA sequencing, and liver metabolomics to evaluate the effects of graded wheat bran fiber levels (total dietary fiber [TDF]: 14.07%, 16.32%, 17.99%, and 18.85%) on fiber digestibility, gut microbiota, and metabolism in EHL, compared with two large white pigs (LW) groups: large LW (LLW, same initial physiological stage as EHL) and small LW (SLW, same initial body weight as EHL). Apparent total tract digestibility (ATTD) of TDF in EHL was unaffected by increasing TDF intake (P > 0.05), whereas ATTD of TDF and insoluble dietary fiber in LLW decreased significantly (P < 0.01). High-fiber diet elevated acetate and butyrate, and total SCFAs in LLW (P < 0.05), but only trended toward higher isobutyrate and isovalerate in EHL (0.05 < P < 0.1). Regardless of diet, EHL exhibited higher colonic microbiota diversity (Simpson, P < 0.05) than LW, whereas richness (Chao and ACE) was unaffected by diet or breed (P > 0.05). Breed was the primary factor shaping swine gut microbiota (P < 0.05), with diet showing a trend toward significance, shaping colonic microbiota (P = 0.0586). Multi-omics integration identified 29 key genera and 10 metabolites associated with high-fiber digestibility in EHL. These key bacteria and metabolites were co-enriched in carbohydrate metabolism pathways, including butanoate metabolism and starch and sucrose metabolism, and collectively contribute to the high-fiber digestibility phenotype.
IMPORTANCE: Indigenous Chinese pig breeds, such as the Erhualian pig (EHL), exhibit a superior capacity for high-fiber tolerance compared with commercial lean-type breeds, which currently account for approximately 90% of China's pig inventory. Reliance on lean-type breeds has increased concentrate feed demand, intensifying human-livestock food competition. While low-cost unconventional feedstuffs (such as rice bran and wheat bran) are available, their high insoluble fiber content limits utilization in modern breeds. Elucidating the mechanisms underlying the high-fiber tolerance of EHL is of critical importance, specifically the gut microbiota, metabolites that enable efficient utilization of higher fiber levels. In this study, we integrated colonic short-chain fatty acid (SCFA), microbiome profiling, liver metabolomics, and functional correlation analyses to demonstrate that the high-fiber digestibility of EHL is associated with breed-specific microbial compositional features and a distinct hepatic metabolic profile, characterized by enrichment of carbohydrate and butanoate metabolism. The integration of microbiota functional prediction and metabolomic data reveals potential microbial-host co-metabolic networks that underpin this phenotype. Collectively, this work will advance understanding of the metabolic and microbial mechanisms underlying high-fiber tolerance, offering potential strategies for improving feed efficiency in monogastric animals through microbiome and metabolic modulation.
